region.text: Surat, where East India Company traders settled

ledger.note: 1608: East India Company traders settle at Surat. The overseas possessions page lists Surat in 1608, where East India Company traders settled, without a prior holder; the Mughal Empire is my reading (Cliopatria's Mughal row touches this row 1662-1720 in the seed). Cliopatria draws four Surat cells only in 1662-1686. [Reviewer am-07-a, 2026-10-19: the same page's timeline lists '1612 Surat, India', against the body's 1608; the conflict was not flagged.]

region.text: Bermuda, settled after the wreck of the Sea Venture

ledger.note: 1609: Bermuda is settled by accident after the Sea Venture wreck. The overseas possessions page: settled by accident after the Sea Venture wreck, official in 1612.

1610: Cuper's Cove is founded in Newfoundland. The overseas possessions page lists Cuper's Cove, Newfoundland, founded 1610 and abandoned in the 1620s. Cliopatria draws the five Conception Bay cells from 1612.
1615: Renews is founded in Newfoundland (page: founded, abandoned 1619). The region is the Newfoundland cells that Cliopatria adds in 1619, my reading.
1617: the London and Bristol Company founds Cambriol in Newfoundland (page: abandoned by 1637). Same Newfoundland cells as Renews; the region is my reading.
1620: the Pilgrims found Plymouth Colony. The Thirteen Colonies page: settled in 1620 by English Puritan separatists (Pilgrims) who sailed on the Mayflower.
1621 (August): the first settlers reach Ferryland, Newfoundland. The overseas possessions page: granted 1620 to Calvert, first settlers August 1621.
1622: the Province of Maine is granted. The page: granted; sold to Massachusetts Bay in 1677. A grant, not a settlement; the region is the Maine coast that Cliopatria draws by 1632, my reading.
1623: New Hampshire is settled (overseas possessions page). The Thirteen Colonies page gives 1629 for New Hampshire's establishment; the region is the coast Cliopatria draws in 1626, my reading.

region.text: Saint Kitts, settled by the English

ledger.note: 1623: the English settle Saint Kitts. The page: settled by the English, the French followed in 1625, Spain seized it in 1629. It does not say when the English came back; the island is shared with France until the French part is ceded in 1713 (Treaty of Utrecht page). Cliopatria draws none of it.
1625: England settles Barbados, a major English settlement (page: first visited by the Olive Blossom in 1605). Cliopatria draws it from 1629.
1628: Nevis is settled (overseas possessions page: Nevis settled 1628). No place name for the island in the gazetteer, hence the coordinate.

1629: Puritans found the Massachusetts Bay Colony. The Thirteen Colonies page: Puritans 'immigrated in 1629 and established the Massachusetts Bay Colony' (its table gives 1628; the other page lists Salem 1628 and Boston 1630).

region.text: Sierra Leone, four cells at about 7.5N 12.7W

ledger.note: 1629: four cells appear in Sierra Leone (7.5N 12.7W) and stay to 1669. Page silent: the overseas possessions page lists only a 1618 trading charter for the Gold Coast and Gambia and does not mention Sierra Leone. Recorded to explain the shape.

1629: the English also seize Acadia and Cape Breton Island. The page: the treaty 'returned New France (Quebec, Acadia and Cape Breton Island) to French control' after the English had seized it in 1629. The page has no month for these and does not mention a Scottish colony; the region (Nova Scotia) is my reading of 'Acadia and Cape Breton'.

1629 (19 July): David Kirke's English fleet takes Quebec. The page: 'On 19 July 1629, an English fleet under the command of David Kirke managed to cause the surrender of Quebec.' It came after the Treaty of Suza, so it was 'considered illegitimate'.
1632: Antigua is settled by colonists from Saint Kitts (overseas possessions page). The Natural Earth country also holds Barbuda, which the page dates to 1666.
1632: Montserrat is settled (overseas possessions page). Cliopatria draws no Montserrat cell.

region.text: Quebec, Acadia and Cape Breton Island

ledger.note: 1632 (29 March): England gives Quebec, Acadia and Cape Breton back at Saint-Germain-en-Laye. The page: the treaty was signed on March 29, 1632 and 'returned New France (Quebec, Acadia and Cape Breton Island) to French control'. The page gives no date for the physical handover.
1634: Maryland is founded. The overseas possessions page: Maryland founded 1634; the Thirteen Colonies page gives only the 1632 charter to Cecil Calvert.
1636: Connecticut is established (page: established 1636, chartered as a royal colony in 1662). The overseas possessions page says 1633.
1636: Roger Williams founds Providence Plantations (page: Roger Williams established Providence Plantations in 1636).
1638: New Haven is founded (overseas possessions page: founded 1638, merged with Connecticut 1665; the Thirteen Colonies page says 1664).

region.text: the village of Madrasapatnam, site of Fort St. George

ledger.note: 1639: the East India Company buys Madrasapatnam and builds Fort St. George. The page: the Company bought the village in 1639, the land grant coming from the Raja of Chandragiri; infobox 'Ceded by Vijaynagar governor: 1639'. the Agency of Fort St. George was established in 1640 and became headquarters on the Coromandel Coast in 1641. Cliopatria's Vijayanagara row ends in 1571, so the counterpart is the page's, not the map's.

region.text: the Gold Coast, two cells at about 5.2N 1.0W

ledger.note: 1640: two cells appear on the Gold Coast. Page silent: the overseas possessions page lists a 1618 charter to an English company for trade in the Gold Coast and Gambia and a 1673 Fort James, but no 1640 post.

region.text: Eleuthera, settled by the Eleutheran Adventurers

ledger.note: 1648: Bermudians, the Eleutheran Adventurers, settle Eleuthera in the Bahamas (page: Eleuthera left to the Eleutheran Adventurers from Bermuda to settle).
1648: Virginia grows from 9 to 46 cells. Page silent: the Thirteen Colonies page says only that Jamestown's early years saw 'wars with local Indians' and names no treaty or boundary.

region.text: the Suriname River, English colony of Lord Willoughby

ledger.note: 1650: Lord Willoughby's colony is founded on the Suriname River. The page: founded in 1650 by Lord Willoughby, set up by Major Anthony Rowse; a first attempt had been made at Marshall's Creek in 1630. Area 'around 30,000 acres (120 km2)'. Cliopatria draws about 20,000 km2 from 1653.

1653: six North Carolina cells appear. Page silent and in conflict: the Thirteen Colonies page gives the Carolina charter as 1663 and says 'Carolina was not settled until 1670'. Kept to explain the shape; the cells may be settlers spreading from Virginia.

1655: England conquers Jamaica from Spain under Cromwell. The overseas possessions page: Jamaica conquered under Oliver Cromwell, formerly the Spanish possession Santiago; the Treaty of Madrid page: 'a successful invasion of Jamaica' after a failed attempt on Hispaniola (no month). Cliopatria draws it from 1659.

region.text: Tangier, part of Catherine of Braganza's dowry

ledger.note: 1661: Tangier comes to England with Catherine of Braganza's dowry. The page: Tangier acquired as part of Catherine of Braganza's dowry, abandoned 1684. Cliopatria draws it from 1662.

region.text: Bombay, part of Catherine of Braganza's dowry

ledger.note: 1661: Bombay is transferred to England in Catherine of Braganza's dowry (page: Bombay transferred to England as part of Catherine's dowry, prior holder Portugal). The Portuguese Empire dossier records the same transfer with the English crown as counterpart.

region.text: Delaware and the old New Sweden land, held by the Dutch

ledger.note: 1664: Delaware and the former New Sweden land are taken from the Dutch. The page lists 1664 Delaware and Pennsylvania (New Sweden) as taken from the Dutch. The page gives no month.

region.text: New Netherland, from Long Island up the Hudson valley

ledger.note: 1664 (27 August): the English fleet takes New Amsterdam. The page: 'New Amsterdam surrendered to Colonel Richard Nicholls on August 27, 1664; he renamed it New York' (infobox 28 August). New Netherland's dossier records the same contest.

region.text: New Netherland: New York, New Jersey and the Hudson valley to Fort Orange (Albany)

ledger.note: 1664 (September): New Netherland is English; the page describes the Duke of York's province as running from Long Island, up the Hudson and Mohawk valleys, to the Great Lakes. The page: Fort Orange capitulated on 24 September (renamed Albany) and the infobox dates the surrender of New Netherland to 29 September 1664; New Jersey was granted to Carteret and Berkeley the same year. Cliopatria draws these cells from 1670.
1664 (29 September): the surrender of New Netherland ends the fighting (infobox: surrender of New Netherland, 29 September 1664).

region.text: Mahim, Sion, Dharavi and Wadala on Bombay

ledger.note: 1665-1666: Mahim, Sion, Dharavi and Wadala are acquired from the Portuguese on Bombay (page: 1665-1666, acquired from the Portuguese). The year is the page's first; the region is the island group around Bombay.

1667: Suriname goes to the Dutch. The page: Admiral Abraham Crijnssen captured it in 1667 and an English fleet under John Harman retook it five months later; the English held it until news of the Treaty of Breda ('signed in July') reached the settlement 'only weeks later'. The exchange was de facto, 'under the terms of the Treaty of Westminster seven years later'. The page also describes commissioners arriving in June 1675 and about 1,100 people removed by early September; its infobox ends the colony in 1667. [Reviewer am-07-a, 2026-10-19: counterpart changed from dutch-republic to dutch-suriname, whose dossier exists and founds the colony on 26 February 1667 with this dossier as counterpart and predecessor.]
1670: the Sierra Leone cells vanish from the shape. Page silent.

region.text: 'all lands within the drainage basin of Hudson's Bay', of which only a post on James Bay is drawn

ledger.note: 1670: Charles II grants the Hudson's Bay Company its charter. The Rupert's Land page: 'In 1670, King Charles II of England granted a royal charter to create the Hudson's Bay Company'; the Governor and Company are 'the true and absolute Lords and Proprietors' of the basin, 'about 3,861,400 square kilometres'. That is a chartered claim, not settled land; only the post drawn by Cliopatria is the gain, the rest should be soft.

1670: Carolina is settled at Charles Town. The Thirteen Colonies page: the royal charter of 1663, but 'Carolina was not settled until 1670'. The Treaty of Madrid page notes a historian's view that the treaty legalised English ownership 'as far south as Charleston'.

region.text: English logwood stations on the coast of the Bay of Honduras

ledger.note: 1670 (8 July): Spain accepts English logwood stations on the coast. The Treaty of Madrid page: the page says Spain accepted new English logwood stations along the coast from Yucatan to Nicaragua without formally recognising them (marked citation needed), and that the treaty set no boundaries and adopted only the principle of actual possession. The overseas possessions page lists Belize under 1638. Cliopatria draws the whole country, which the shape correction cuts.
1673: the shape draws 44 Bahamas cells. Page silent: the overseas possessions page dates only Eleuthera (1648) and Turks and Caicos (1670, listed).
1673: Fort James, Ghana, is listed as an English possession (overseas possessions page). Accra for Fort James is my reading. Cliopatria's Gold Coast cells grow to 12 by 1700.

region.text: New York and the Hudson valley, retaken by the Dutch

ledger.note: 1673 (July): a Dutch fleet retakes New York. The page: Governor Francis Lovelace held office 'until the return of the Dutch in July 1673'; the Dutch held it until the Treaty of Westminster returned it to the English.

region.text: New York and the Hudson valley, returned to the English

ledger.note: 1674 (5 March): the Treaty of Westminster returns New York to England (infobox: Treaty of Westminster, 5 March 1674); the Duke of York gets a second grant in July 1674 and appoints Edmund Andros governor. The New Netherland dossier dates the physical handover to 10 November 1674 (not read here).

1681: William Penn's Pennsylvania is founded (page: founded in 1681 as a proprietary colony). The overseas possessions page adds Philadelphia in 1682 and calls the land first settled by Dutch and Swedes.
1684: England abandons Tangier (page: abandoned 1684). Morocco as the taker is my reading: Cliopatria's Morocco row touches this row 1670-1686 in the seed. Cliopatria drops the cells in 1687.
1687: the four Surat cells vanish from the shape. Page silent; the Mughal Empire as taker is my reading.
1687: Virginia grows from 53 to 84 cells. Page silent.

region.text: a post on the south-west shore of Hudson Bay at about 57N 92.5W

ledger.note: 1687: a Hudson Bay post at about 57N 92.5W enters the shape. The Rupert's Land page dates no posts.

1690: the East India Company settles Calcutta (page: Calcutta, Bengal, settled by the East India Company in 1690). The page names no prior holder; the Mughal Empire is my reading (Cliopatria's Mughal row touches this row 1662-1720). Cliopatria draws it from 1691.
1696: the Hudson Bay post at 57N leaves the shape. Page silent on the date; the Treaty of Utrecht page has France cede 'territories in Rupert's Land' in 1713, which implies French holds earlier.
1702: Carolina grows from 10 to 22 cells and Virginia by three; a James Bay post at 52.3N 82W appears. Page silent (the Thirteen Colonies page notes only that Carolina was split in 1712).
1707: the English colonies become British. The page: the Acts of Union create Great Britain and the English colonies become British colonies. Colour and dossier continue.

region.text: the Atlantic, Caribbean and African colonies of the 1712 shape

ledger.note: 1713: the colonies pass to the British Colonial Empire row. Cliopatria's bookkeeping, not a loss: that row already draws 771 of this shape's 777 cells in 1709-1712 and grows in 1713 with the cessions of the Treaty of Utrecht (11 April 1713: 'ceded Nova Scotia and its claims to Newfoundland and territories in Rupert's Land'; 'the French portion of Saint Kitts'). The page does not mention the row split.
1762: Bombay is carried by the British Empire row (which draws Madras, Bombay and Masulipatnam in 1762); this row has no 1762 shape. Page silent.

1763: the Chingleput jaghire becomes the Madras presidency's first district (page: it was obtained in 1763). The Carnatic Sultanate as the grantor is my reading (the page names the Nawab of Arcot only for the 1801 treaty). Cliopatria does not draw it.

1763: two cells at Masulipatnam enter the shape. Page silent: the Madras Presidency page says only that the factory dates 'back to 1611'. Hyderabad State as the holder is my reading (Cliopatria's Hyderabad row touches this row 1763-1768).
1778: Masulipatnam leaves this row's shape; the British Empire row has drawn it since 1769. Page silent.

region.text: Madras (Fort St. George), the last land of the row

ledger.note: 1779: the last shape of the row ends; the British Empire row draws Madras from 1780. Not a historical end: the English colonies became British in 1707 (colour continues in the successors). Page silent on 1779.

wars.name: Anglo-French War (1627-1629)

zones.text: Quebec, Acadia and Cape Breton Island

wars.outcome: An English fleet under David Kirke took Quebec on 19 July 1629 and the English seized Acadia and Cape Breton; the Treaty of Saint-Germain-en-Laye of 29 March 1632 returned all of New France to France.
wars.note: The page gives the war only by its title years (1627-1629). The surrender of Quebec came after the Treaty of Suza and 'considered illegitimate'; 'to' is the treaty year 1632, when the land was returned.

wars.name: Anglo-Spanish War (1654-1660)
wars.outcome: England joined France against Spain in late 1654, failed at Hispaniola and took Jamaica; in the Caribbean the war went on as privateer raids until the Treaty of Madrid of 8 July 1670, which adopted only the principle of actual possession.
wars.note: The page says there was no England-Spain treaty in 1660 (the Treaty of the Pyrenees was France-Spain), hence 'to' is 1670. Morgan's raid on Panama City (28 January 1671) came before news of the treaty arrived.

wars.name: Second Anglo-Dutch War

zones.text: New Netherland, taken by the English in August-September 1664
the Suriname colony, taken by Crijnssen and retaken by Harman in 1667

wars.outcome: England took New Netherland (27 August to 29 September 1664); the Dutch took Suriname in 1667 and the English retook it five months later; the Treaty of Breda was signed in July 1667, and the exchange of Suriname for New York was only de facto, 'under the terms of the Treaty of Westminster seven years later'.
wars.note: Neither page opened (this and the Province of New York page) names the war; the title is the usual English one. The 1664 dates are from the Province of New York page.

wars.name: Third Anglo-Dutch War

zones.text: New York and the Hudson valley, Dutch from July 1673

wars.outcome: A Dutch fleet recaptured New York in July 1673; the Treaty of Westminster of 5 March 1674 returned it to England.
wars.note: The page does not name the war; the title is the usual English one. The Dutch hold lasted from July 1673 to the treaty; Cliopatria's shape does not show the interruption.

wars.name: War of the Spanish Succession
wars.outcome: The Treaty of Utrecht (main treaties of 11 April 1713) gave Britain Nova Scotia, claims to Newfoundland, 'territories in Rupert's Land' and the French part of Saint Kitts, and Gibraltar and Menorca from Spain (13 July 1713).
wars.note: Zones are empty because the cessions are drawn by the British Colonial Empire row, which carries the Atlantic colonies from 1713. The page opened gives no start year: 1702 is the year of Cliopatria's shape change (Carolina growth, the St. Augustine cells), not a page's.

certainty.note: Colonial frontiers are charter claims and settled enclaves, not surveyed lines: the Treaty of Madrid page says the treaty of 8 July 1670 set no boundaries and adopted only the principle of actual possession. Island colonies (Bermuda, Barbados, Antigua, Jamaica, the Bahamas) have natural coasts; Rupert's Land is a claim to a basin.
Madras, Bombay and Masulipatnam are small company enclaves round forts; their limits follow grants (the Chingleput jaghire of 1763) and were not surveyed.

notes:
WHAT THE ROW IS. Cliopatria's 'English Colonial Empire' (1609-1779, 27 shapes) is a composite, not one state: 1609-1712 it draws the English Atlantic, Caribbean, West African and Indian possessions (Virginia, Bermuda, Newfoundland, New England, Maryland, Jamaica, Barbados, Antigua, Suriname 1653-1669, Belize, the Bahamas, Carolina, New York and the Jerseys, Pennsylvania, Hudson Bay posts, Tangier, Bombay, Surat, Calcutta, Cape Coast); from 1713 it keeps only Madras and Bombay (to 1761) and Masulipatnam (1763-1777). Type 'colony', family 'britain'; the metropole is the Kingdom of England (kingdom-of-england, then Great Britain from 1707): the colony relation belongs in that dossier. The state is dated from Jamestown (14 May 1607, Thirteen Colonies page), two years before Cliopatria; it ends 1779 only because the row does.

CLIOPATRIA ROWS TO MERGE OR CLEAN. (1) 'British Colonial Empire' draws 771 of this row's 777 cells in 1709-1712 and alone from 1713: the colonies are double-drawn four years and the 1713 'loss' is a hand-over, not a historical event (ledger: split, confidence 1). The two dossiers (this one and eu-11's) should agree that the English phase ends with the 1707 rename. (2) 'British Empire' draws Madras, Bombay and Masulipatnam in 1762 (this row has no 1762 shape), Bombay 1763-1779 and Masulipatnam 1769-1779: Masulipatnam is double-drawn 1769-1777 and Bombay 1763-1777. (3) The Willoughbyland block is about 160 times too large. (4) Belize is drawn whole (76 cells) from 1670. (5) Four St. Augustine cells 1702-1712 are on Spanish land. (6) St Kitts, Nevis and Montserrat are not drawn at all.

PAGE BUDGET. Nine pages were opened (the budget for 27 shapes). Verified from them: the founding or acquisition years of Jamestown, Bermuda, Newfoundland, Plymouth, Massachusetts, Maine, New Hampshire, Saint Kitts, Barbados, Nevis, Antigua, Montserrat, Maryland, Connecticut, Rhode Island, New Haven, Madras, Eleuthera, Suriname, Jamaica, Tangier, Bombay, New Netherland, Charleston, Pennsylvania, Calcutta; the Kirke episode of Quebec; the Dutch interruptions of 1667 and 1673-74; the 1713 treaties. Unverified: page budget: Virginia's growth in 1648 and 1687 and the cell-level growth of New England and Maryland, the Sierra Leone and Gold Coast cells (1629-1669, 1640-1702), the Bahamas beyond Eleuthera (1673), the Hudson Bay posts (1670, 1687, 1696, 1702), the Boston cells of 1622, the North Carolina cells of 1653, the New York cell of 1640, Surat 1662-1686, Masulipatnam 1763-1777, the St. Augustine cells of 1702. Each carries a confidence-1 event or a keyframe note saying so.

DISAGREEMENTS BETWEEN PAGES. Connecticut 1633 (overseas possessions) vs 1636 (Thirteen Colonies); New Hampshire 1623 vs 1629; New Haven merged 1665 vs 1664; Massachusetts Bay 1628 (table) vs 1629 (text) vs Boston 1630; Maine sold to Massachusetts Bay in 1677 vs absorbed by 1658; Willoughbyland ends 1667 (infobox, Breda) vs a removal of 1,100 people in June-September 1675; Province of New York crown colony 1685 (text) vs 1689 (infobox); Dominion of New England 1685 vs 1686-1689; Madras presidency 1784 vs 1785. The Treaty of Westminster is 5 March 1674 on the New York page; the New Netherland dossier records a handover on 10 November 1674.

LISTED ON THE PAGES AND NOT DRAWN OR ADDED. From the overseas possessions page: the Popham Colony in Maine (13 August 1607, abandoned after about a year), Cape Ann 1624, Providence Island (1629, captured by Spain 1641), the Mosquito Coast (1630), Anguilla (1650), Saint Lucia (1663), Barbuda (1666), the Cayman Islands (1670), Turks and Caicos (1670), the British Virgin Islands (1672), Fort Gambia (1661, ceded 1664), Bantam, Run (1616-1665), Bencoolen (1685), Machilipatnam (1611). From the Madras page: Fort St. David (acquired 1690), the French capture of Madras (September 1746, returned 1749). They are tiny, short-lived or undated; a gap-filler with a page budget could add the Bahamas' New Providence, Providence Island, Anguilla and the Gambia.

RUPERT'S LAND. The charter of 1670 (Rupert's Land page) grants the whole Hudson Bay basin (3.86 M km2, seventeen times this row's largest shape). It is a chartered claim, mostly Native land, and is not drawn; the ledger's gain is limited to the post that Cliopatria draws. A rendering rule for claims (soft outline) would suit it; the Treaty of Utrecht page has France cede 'territories in Rupert's Land' in 1713, so French and English posts shared the bay.

SAINT KITTS. The English share is drawn as the whole island in every corrected shape because Cliopatria has no French Saint-Christophe row; the Treaty of Utrecht page cedes 'the French portion of Saint Kitts' in 1713. A dossier for French Saint-Christophe (1625-1713) would let the two be separated.

PRIOR HOLDERS I HAD TO READ INTO THE PAGES. Mughal Empire for Surat and Calcutta, Hyderabad State for Masulipatnam, Carnatic Sultanate for the Chingleput jaghire, Morocco for Tangier: each is marked confidence 2 or 1 in the ledger, with the seed's neighbour years as the evidence. Vijayanagara Empire for Madras follows the page's infobox ('Ceded by Vijaynagar governor: 1639') although Cliopatria's row ends in 1571.

GAZETTEER NAMES. Not found and replaced by intersections with the Cliopatria shape or by coordinates: Cuper's Cove (Cupids), Renews, Ferryland (Newfoundland), Chingleput (Chengalpattu), Sherbro/Bunce Island (Sierra Leone), Nevis (as a place), Jamestown (Virginia; the gazetteer's three Jamestowns are not the Virginia one, so a 35 km disc round 37.21N 76.78W is used), Hudson Bay as a place (the gazetteer's 'Hudson Bay' is a Saskatchewan town; a 120 km disc round 57.0N 92.6W is used for the York Factory area), Portsmouth (New Hampshire), Cape Breton, Salsette.
